fullDesc: Learn to use Google Search Console to diagnose indexing issues, monitor search performance and identify actionable opportunities for organic visibility. Build practical skills in Search Console reporting, technical issue identification, Google AI-search visibility analysis and data-driven SEO recommendations. This focused 4-week, 24-hour certification course teaches property verification, sitemap submissions, URL inspection, crawl diagnostics, canonicalization, Core Web Vitals interpretation, PageSpeed Insights analysis, and modern Generative AI Performance reporting. Students build an end-to-end SEO Audit & 30-Day Visibility Improvement Plan using real or guided demonstration properties.
overview: The Google Search Console & SEO Reporting certification course provides a rigorous, hands-on foundation in Google's official search diagnostic platform. Moving beyond guesswork and generic SEO checklists, the programme equips marketers, website managers, content publishers, and freelancers with the diagnostic competencies needed to inspect indexing pipelines, uncover high-opportunity search queries, audit page-experience signals, evaluate Google AI Overviews and AI Mode impressions, and present stakeholder-ready SEO reporting dashboards.
why_now: With continuous Google Search updates, expanding AI Overviews, and strict technical indexing criteria, website visibility depends directly on first-party search telemetry. Google Search Console is the single authoritative source of truth provided directly by Google to webmasters. Understanding how Google crawls, indexes, and serves content—and how to communicate diagnostic findings to developers and clients—is an indispensable skill for every modern digital marketer, SEO practitioner, and site owner.

modules.title: Setup, Verification & Search Console Fundamentals
modules.objective: Establish property ownership, configure user permissions, navigate the Search Console interface, and conduct an initial property-health baseline audit.
topics: Google Search Console fundamentals: the official bridge between Google's indexing system and webmasters; why GSC is essential for modern organic search visibility
Domain properties versus URL-prefix properties: DNS-level verification vs. protocol/subdomain-specific scoping; choosing the right property type for your website architecture
Ownership verification methods: DNS TXT records, HTML file upload, HTML tag injection, Google Tag Manager container, and Google Analytics linking; managing verification risks
Property settings, access management, and permission tiers: Owner (Full/Delegated), Full User, and Restricted User permissions; security best practices for agency and client access
Search Console dashboard navigation and initial property-health checklist: overview tab, notifications center, security & manual actions alerts, and baseline configuration review
modules.hands_on_practice: Setting up or inspecting an authorized Search Console property, verifying ownership via preferred methods, configuring user access roles, and documenting an initial 10-point property health checklist.
modules.assignment: Search Console Property Setup & Health Baseline Checklist (Google Sheets / PDF) confirming property scoping, verification method, permission audit, and initial health observations.
modules.assessment_criteria: Correct selection of property type, valid verification documentation, appropriate user permission assignment, and thoroughness of the initial health audit checklist.

modules.title: Indexing, Crawling & URL Diagnostics
modules.objective: Inspect Google's crawling and indexing pipelines, evaluate sitemaps, interpret indexing exclusions, and diagnose URL status using the URL Inspection tool.
topics: Google's crawling, indexing, and serving fundamentals: the distinction between discovery, crawl requests, page processing, indexing eligibility, and search serving
XML sitemaps and sitemap submission: standard XML sitemaps, sitemap index files, best practices, submission workflows, and reading sitemap processing status and error codes
Page indexing reports and exclusion reasons: deep dive into 'Discovered - currently not indexed', 'Crawled - currently not indexed', 'Excluded by ‘noindex’ tag', 'Page with redirect', and 'Soft 404'
URL Inspection tool mastery: retrieving live Google index status, inspecting referring pages, crawl timestamps, user-agent details, HTTP response codes, and rendering screenshots
Canonical URL observations and duplicate-content diagnostics: User-declared canonical vs. Google-selected canonical; diagnosing mismatches, canonical overrides, and parameter sprawl
Identifying crawl-discovery issues and fix validation: requesting re-indexing, monitoring issue validation cycles, and distinguishing diagnostic findings from developer code fixes
hands_on_tools: Google Search Console Page Indexing Report
modules.hands_on_practice: Running 5 target URLs through the URL Inspection tool, comparing user vs. Google-selected canonicals, categorizing indexing exclusions from the Page Indexing report, and drafting diagnostic tickets.
modules.assignment: Indexing Issue Register & URL Diagnostic Audit (Google Sheets / PDF) categorizing at least 5 distinct URL indexing issues with category, technical evidence, severity priority, and recommended remediation.
modules.assessment_criteria: Accurate categorization of indexing exclusions, correct interpretation of URL Inspection telemetry, and actionable, technically precise remediation recommendations.

modules.title: Search Performance Analysis & SEO Opportunities
modules.objective: Analyze organic search telemetry—queries, pages, impressions, clicks, CTR, and average position—to uncover high-intent keyword opportunities and optimize CTR.
topics: Understanding core search metrics: Clicks (user visits), Impressions (search results viewed), Click-Through Rate (CTR = Clicks / Impressions), and Average Position (mean top ranking)
Query-level and page-level performance analysis: evaluating top organic search queries, landing page performance, and query-to-page alignment
Segmentation dimensions: analyzing performance by Countries (geographic demand), Devices (desktop vs. mobile vs. tablet), Dates (seasonality), and Search Appearance (rich results, snippets)
Period comparison and trend analysis: comparing 28-day, 3-month, and year-over-year performance; identifying rising queries, decaying keywords, and seasonal search shifts
Identifying high-impression, low-CTR opportunities: spotting pages ranking on page 1 with substandard CTR; title tag and meta description optimization strategies to capture clicks
Interpreting branded versus non-branded search patterns: separating brand navigation queries from unbranded discovery traffic to evaluate true organic acquisition health
Exporting Search Console data: downloading query and page reports to Google Sheets for advanced filtering, pivot tables, and statistical ranking distributions
modules.hands_on_practice: Applying regex filters in GSC Performance report to isolate non-branded questions, exporting query data to Google Sheets, and building a high-impression low-CTR opportunity matrix.
modules.assignment: Organic Search Performance & Keyword Opportunity Report (Google Sheets / PDF) highlighting top 10 winning queries, 5 decaying pages, and 5 high-impression low-CTR optimization opportunities with revised titles and snippets.
competencies: Search metric interpretation (Clicks, Impressions, CTR, Position)
modules.assessment_criteria: Precision of data filtering, analytical depth of query observations, correct identification of high-impression low-CTR targets, and quality of proposed optimization recommendations.

modules.title: Technical Monitoring & Reporting
modules.objective: Evaluate page experience and technical quality signals, interpret Core Web Vitals, monitor structured data enhancements, and construct automated SEO reporting tables.
topics: Core Web Vitals report interpretation: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) in Search Console
PageSpeed Insights diagnostic integration: understanding field data (Chrome User Experience Report / CrUX) vs. lab data (Lighthouse); identifying render-blocking scripts and layout shifts
HTTPS, mobile usability history, and page experience monitoring: verifying security protocols, mixed content issues, and site-wide HTTPS compliance
Structured data enhancement reports: inspecting schema markups (Articles, Breadcrumbs, FAQs, Products, Sitelinks Searchbox) and resolving invalid item warnings
Issue validation and monitoring history: initiating fix validation in GSC, tracking Google's re-crawl status, and verifying resolution timelines
Building technical reporting tables and charts in Google Sheets: creating monthly technical health dashboards with conditional formatting and severity tracking
Looker Studio SEO dashboard introduction: connecting Google Search Console connector to Looker Studio for executive automated reporting
hands_on_tools: Google Search Console Core Web Vitals Report
modules.hands_on_practice: Auditing a website's Core Web Vitals status in GSC, running PageSpeed diagnostic tests on flagged URLs, inspecting structured data warnings, and building an automated Google Sheets technical tracker.
modules.assignment: Technical SEO Monitoring Dashboard & Issue-Priority Register (Google Sheets / Looker Studio) tracking Core Web Vitals URLs, HTTPS status, schema validation results, and categorized developer tickets.
competencies: Core Web Vitals interpretation (LCP, INP, CLS)
Technical SEO reporting & Looker Studio basics
modules.assessment_criteria: Correct interpretation of CrUX field metrics, accurate identification of schema warnings, clean visual reporting layout, and proper prioritization of technical issues.

modules.title: AI Search Reporting, Analysis & Action Planning
modules.objective: Analyze Google Generative AI Search Performance reports, evaluate AI Overviews impressions and limitations, and synthesize all diagnostic data into a 30-day SEO action plan.
topics: Introduction to Google Search generative AI visibility: how generative AI features (AI Overviews and AI Mode) display synthesized summaries in Google Search results
Understanding the Generative AI Performance report in Search Console: background of the June 2026 introduction and August 31, 2026 worldwide rollout; eligibility criteria and impression thresholds
AI Overviews and AI Mode visibility reporting: identifying queries and landing pages cited or featured within generative AI summaries
Understanding eligible dimensions: analyzing AI Search data across pages, countries, devices, and dates

Interpreting AI impressions, reporting limitations, and data availability: why individual properties may show zero data; understanding that GSC does NOT provide separate AI clicks, CTR, average rank position, or prompt logs
Generative AI reporting for Google Discover: overview of AI features in Discover feeds and differences from Search performance
Traditional Search performance versus AI-feature reporting: comparing standard web search metrics against generative AI impression volume; avoiding manufactured ranking metrics
Data exports, anomaly investigation, and evidence-based interpretation: auditing unexpected traffic shifts, AI summary inclusion drops, and data discrepancies
Preparing client-ready SEO reporting summaries: synthesizing technical diagnostics, keyword wins, and AI visibility into executive-level narratives
Building a prioritized 30-day monitoring and improvement plan: structuring weekly milestones for crawl fixes, CTR tests, Core Web Vitals collaboration, and monthly re-audits
hands_on_tools: Google Search Console Generative AI Report (or illustrative dataset)
modules.hands_on_practice: Analyzing Generative AI Performance data (or an explicitly labeled illustrative training dataset), identifying cited pages, documenting data limitations, and authoring a 30-day SEO action plan.
modules.assignment: Final Capstone Deliverable: Google Search Console SEO Audit & 30-Day Visibility Improvement Plan synthesizing property setup, indexing register, search opportunities, AI observations, and weekly milestones.
modules.assessment_criteria: Factual accuracy regarding AI search reporting limitations (no fabricated clicks/ranks), thoroughness of the final audit, and practical feasibility of the 30-day action plan.

faq.question: What will I learn in this Google Search Console course?
faq.answer: You will learn property setup and verification, page indexing diagnostics, crawl error troubleshooting, organic search performance analysis (clicks, impressions, CTR, position), Core Web Vitals monitoring, and how to interpret modern Google Generative AI Search Performance reports to build actionable SEO recommendations.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The course begins with foundational concepts of how search engines crawl, index, and serve web pages. Basic computer literacy and internet navigation skills are all that is required. No programming, HTML, or prior web development background is needed.

faq.question: Does this course include practical projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Students complete hands-on practical labs including an Indexing Issue Register, a Search Performance Opportunity Report, and a comprehensive final Capstone: the Google Search Console SEO Audit & 30-Day Visibility Improvement Plan.

faq.question: Will I learn Google AI Overviews and AI Mode reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers the dedicated Generative AI Performance report introduced by Google in 2026. You will learn to analyze eligible dimensions (pages, countries, devices, dates) and understand critical reporting limitations, such as why Google does not provide separate click counts, CTR, average rank position, or search prompts for generative features.

faq.question: Do I need my own website?
faq.answer: An authorized website is ideal, but not mandatory. Nova Skills provides a guided demonstration workflow and prepared diagnostic datasets so that students without direct property access can complete all exercises and portfolio deliverables.

faq.question: Is this a complete SEO course?
faq.answer: No. This is a focused certification dedicated specifically to Google Search Console diagnostics, technical monitoring, and SEO performance reporting. Complete strategic SEO, on-page content strategy, link building, and advanced technical engineering are covered in Course 33: SEO & AI Search Optimization.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is 4 Weeks (24 total learning hours across 5 structured modules, requiring approximately 6 hours per week). The course tuition is an institutional fee of ₹3,900 (plus applicable GST). In accordance with Nova Skills Truth in Pricing policy, there are no fake discounts or countdown markups.

faq.question: Will I receive a certificate?
faq.answer: Yes. Students who successfully complete the coursework and submit the mandatory capstone project receive a Nova Skills Course Completion Certificate as a Google Search Console & SEO Reporting Specialist. Please note this is an institutional credential and not an official certificate issued by Google LLC.

faq.question: What is the difference between Google Search Console and Google Analytics 4?
faq.answer: Google Search Console focuses on how your website performs in Google Search before users click (impressions, search queries, rankings, indexing health, and crawl diagnostics). Google Analytics 4 tracks what users do after they arrive on your website (engagement, bounce rate, pages viewed, conversions, and revenue).

faq.question: What is the URL Inspection tool used for?
faq.answer: The URL Inspection tool is a built-in feature of Google Search Console that allows you to inspect a specific page's status in the Google index, view the last crawl date, inspect canonical declarations, view rendering screenshots, and request fresh indexing after making site updates.

faq.question: Does this course cover Core Web Vitals?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 04 covers the Core Web Vitals report in Search Console (LCP, INP, CLS) and shows how to correlate Search Console data with PageSpeed Insights diagnostics to pinpoint layout shifts and render-blocking resources.

faq.question: What tools will I use throughout the course?
faq.answer: The primary tools are Google Search Console and Google Sheets. Supporting tools include Looker Studio (for automated dashboarding), PageSpeed Insights (for speed diagnostics), and the built-in GSC URL Inspection tool.
